chunks: And from him, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It was said to him, 'So-and-so married a woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah).' It was said to him, 'She has a husband.' So he asked her. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'And why did he ask her?'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on asking about a woman's marital status before temporary marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the redundant inquiry into a woman's marital status during temporary marriage (*Mut'ah*), implying that such verification is either unnecessary if the status is known or that the focus should remain on the contract's validity rather than procedural checks. This highlights the Shia juristic view that *Mut'ah* does not require the same preconditions as permanent marriage regarding the woman's prior consent or status disclosure, provided the essential elements of the contract are met. The Imam's rhetorical question underscores the flexibility and distinct legal framework of *Mut'ah* within Shia fiqh.
